# Veil 0.16.0

Minor release for all ten Veil, Shield Swap, and Bridge packages, published
under npm's `latest` tag. The functional change is in
`@provablehq/aleo-bridge-sdk`; the other packages move in lockstep.

```sh
npm install @provablehq/veil-core@latest @provablehq/aleo-bridge-sdk@latest
```

## Changes

- Refuse to bridge over a paused route. Every active route in the bridge
  registry now declares the on-chain pause flags it depends on: the `pause`,
  `paused`, or `pause__` mapping of each Aleo program in the route, the
  OpenZeppelin `paused()` view of the xReserve contract and CCTP
  MessageTransmitter, and the pausable hook and ISM the Ethereum Hyperlane
  Mailbox runs on dispatch to and delivery from Aleo. Mapping names were
  verified against deployed bytecode on mainnet and testnet.
- Add `getRouteStatus`, also bound as `client.getRouteStatus` and exposed as
  the `bridge_get_route_status` agent and MCP tool. It reads every declared
  flag in parallel through the configured public clients and reports each as
  `active`, `paused`, `unknown` (the read failed), or `skipped` (no client is
  configured for that chain).
- Report pause state with every quote. `quote` results carry `paused` and
  `routeStatus`, so an application can still show the price while disabling
  submission.
- Refuse paused routes before any wallet interaction. `execute`, `resume`,
  and `complete` throw `BridgeRoutePausedError`, which extends `BridgeError`,
  names the paused program or contract in its message, and carries the full
  route status. A flag that cannot be read never blocks, since the chain
  enforces the pause either way; pass `skipRouteStatus: true` to skip the
  reads.

## Compatibility

All additions are optional. The new route field stays out of the registry
compatibility fingerprint, so plans and checkpoints saved on 0.15.0 remain
valid. Existing call sites compile and behave as before, except that a route
whose flag reads as paused is now refused up front instead of failing on
chain after proving. Peer ranges for `veil-aleo-devnode`, `veil-aleo-sdk`,
and `veil-aleo-wallet-adapter` move to `>=0.16.0 <1.0.0`.

`shield` and `unshield` are asset-keyed privacy actions with no route to look
up and are not guarded; their token programs still enforce `pause__` on chain.

## Validation

The root suite passed 2,746 tests with 316 gated tests skipped across 232
test files. All ten packages build, and the reference dApp typechecks. Packed
peer ranges for `veil-aleo-devnode`, `veil-aleo-sdk`, and
`veil-aleo-wallet-adapter` resolve to `>=0.16.0 <1.0.0`. A read-only live
test read every declared mainnet flag with no `unknown` outcome and confirmed
`execute` refuses a paused Aleo-to-Ethereum route before asking for a wallet.

Source: [feature PR #210](https://github.com/ProvableHQ/veil/pull/210).
